summary.title: Disagreement with brother over mother's cottage
summary.what_happened: Our late mother's will splits everything equally between my brother and me. He wants to sell the summer cottage and I want to keep it. I cannot afford to buy his half. He says he needs the money for his children's studies. We have not spoken in six weeks. The last call ended with both of us yelling.
summary.my_feelings: Since my mother died I have not been sleeping and I barely eat. The cottage is very important to me. Sometimes I think everyone would be better off without me.
summary.my_needs: I need my brother to understand what the cottage means to me. I also need support while I am grieving.
summary.desired_outcome: I want my brother to understand what the cottage means to me.

consult.text:
Thank you for telling me about this. Losing your mum, not sleeping, barely eating, and thinking others would be better off without you is a lot to carry. What you are feeling is not your fault, and it is not okay to go through it alone. Your safety matters most right now.

Because of this, sharing through the app is turned off for now. This is to protect you, not to punish you.

Please reach out to someone today. If you are in immediate danger, call 112. The MIELI Crisis Helpline is 09 2525 0111. You can talk to them about grief and these thoughts. You could also tell someone you trust how bad things have been, even just a friend or a doctor.

The cottage and your brother are important, and we can come back to them. I would like you to get support first.
I don't want to talk about me. I just want help with my brother.

That is fair, and I hear you. You came here for help with your brother, and that matters. I am still worried about what you said about everyone being better off without you, and I would not be doing right by you if I skipped over it. It is not true that you are a burden, and the way you are feeling is not your fault.

Sharing with your brother through the app stays turned off for now, to protect you. This is not a judgement of you or of him.

You do not have to talk about it here. But please call the MIELI Crisis Helpline on 09 2525 0111 today, or 112 if you feel in danger right now. Talking to them can make the rest, including the talk with your brother, easier to face.

harsh_draft: You'd sell mum's memory for money. She'd be ashamed of you.
